clue.text: Country painting's right to replace motorway

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in country life

indicators.note: to replace says one letter is swapped out of the painting word and another put in its place

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: An art critic notes that a landscape picture has had its motorway painted over with something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Country and rural both describe things belonging to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Botched metrication by English, after which response is expected

indicators.note: botched means bungled, so the letters of metrication are jumbled

explanation.surface: The English made a mess of going metric, and now a backlash is due.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaction time is the interval after a stimulus by the end of which a response is made.

clue.text: What drunkard needs when he's in pub and it's all over

indicators.note: all over means turned over completely, so the whole thing is read backwards
in puts the man inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or a drinking room in one
he is taken as written, the 's being is

explanation.surface: A drunkard is in the pub and his drinking days are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's all over' reads the whole pub-with-man assembly backwards; the clue's surface drunkard is the very person who needs the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab, short for rehabilitation, is treatment to help an alcoholic stop drinking.

clue.text: Tea before it's put in bags like so many paper folders?

definitions.text: Tea before it's put in bags
definitions.meaning: tea sold as loose leaves rather than in teabags
a ring binder takes separate sheets that can be removed and added

explanation.surface: Tea that has not yet been bagged sits beside piles of stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-leaf describes both unbagged tea leaves and binders holding removable sheets of paper.

clue.text: Picture one's to move in

definitions.meaning: to picture something in words is to depict or portray it
in geometry a point traces or moves in a path, as when a planet is said to trace an ellipse

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the flat they are about to move into.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the technical one: a moving body is said to trace out the curve it moves in, as a planet traces an ellipse; 'one's to' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to depict in words, and to trace out a path or curve by moving along it.

clue.text: Gloomy face worn by Sergeant Major

indicators.note: worn by says the face sits round the sergeant major, as clothing round a wearer

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: A sergeant major wears a sullen expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means depressing or gloomy, as dismal weather.

clue.text: Game difficult to deal with for Scots on board?

indicators.note: on board here is aboard, so the Scots word goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and SS stands for steamship

parts.words: difficult to deal with for Scots
parts.note: kittle is a Scots word for tricky or difficult to handle

explanation.surface: Scots on a ship find a certain game hard to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: KITTLE is Scots for awkward or ticklish; being on board means being inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles is a game of knocking down wooden pins with a ball.

clue.text: Intensely desirous to lose grammes, becoming tall and thin

indicators.note: to lose says a letter is dropped from the greedy word

parts.note: greedy means having an intense desire for something
G is the abbreviation for grammes

explanation.surface: A greedy person eager to shed weight ends up lanky.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy describes a person who is tall and thin, like a reed.

clue.text: Publisher's past catalogue contains fifty names of those rejected

indicators.note: contains says the catalogue holds the Roman numeral inside it

parts.note: a backlist is a publisher's list of older titles still in print
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An old publisher's catalogue lists fifty authors whose work was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacklist is a list of people or things that are banned or rejected.

clue.text: Shop has run out, after which Eire's lacking new collection of lines

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the first words are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the country Ireland

explanation.surface: A shop has sold out of something, and then the Irish run short of a new batch of lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles the shop letters; 'lacking' drops N from the country name; 'after which' just orders the pieces. The collection is A. E. Housman's 1896 book of poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman's A Shropshire Lad is a famous collection of poems, and poems are made of lines of verse.

clue.text: Robin eagerly played Beatles hit

indicators.note: played suggests a performance, but here signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Robin keenly performed a Beatles song.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor Rigby is a 1966 Beatles single, a hit record about lonely people.

clue.text: Girl walled in by stone slab which is put in cellar

indicators.note: walled in by says the girl's name sits inside the slab

parts.note: a tablet is a flat slab of stone bearing an inscription
Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally

explanation.surface: A girl is bricked up inside a stone slab and left in a wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: The cellar is a salt cellar, the small dish or shaker for salt at table, not a wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar is the vessel that holds ordinary cooking salt at the table.

clue.text: Peasant has only a pair of draught animals left

parts.note: a yoke is a pair of oxen harnessed together

explanation.surface: A poor farmer is down to his last two oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic or peasant.

clue.text: Some corduroy's terrible colour

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fashion critic complains that the shade of some corduroy is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster is a pale greyish-white shade named after the shellfish, used for fabrics and paint.

clue.text: Base depot ordered fast transport

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval base depot orders a quick vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a fast motorboat, a means of rapid water transport.

clue.text: Speedwell I note in North Italian city

indicators.note: in says the letters for I and note go inside the name of the city

parts.note: Verona is a city in northern Italy
C is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone notes having seen a small blue flower growing in a city of northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the botanical genus name for the speedwells, small blue-flowered plants.

clue.text: Butterfly's old distribution area — it's moving north with pressure

parts.note: a range is the area over which a species is found

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving north means read upwards, so the letters are backwards

parts.note: it is taken as written, the 's being is
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that a butterfly's former habitat is shifting north under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving north' turns IT into TI in this down answer. The definition is 'Butterfly's', meaning butterfly is: the 's links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a European butterfly whose males have orange-tipped forewings.

clue.text: Boss shaken by Conservative tale of woe

indicators.note: shaken means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A boss rattled by a Conservative politician pours out his troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of personal hardship told to win sympathy.

clue.text: Amphibian has to walk laboriously about coral structure

indicators.note: about says the trudging word goes round the coral structure

parts.note: to trog is British slang for to trudge or walk wearily
a reef is a ridge built up of coral

explanation.surface: A frog or newt has to plod round a coral reef.
explanation.walkthrough: TROG is informal British for trudging along.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree frog is a frog adapted to climbing, and frogs are amphibians.

clue.text: Military display has tasteless items as well

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods or junk
too means as well or also

explanation.surface: A military parade also features some tacky souvenirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Military sense: the Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous evening display of marching bands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military display of drumming, marching and music.

clue.text: Those who are not soldiers turn up to register as unemployed

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: non-GIs are people who are not American soldiers

explanation.surface: Civilians appear at the job centre to claim benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign on is British for registering to claim unemployment benefit.

clue.text: Precocious girl, twice a mother

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
dam is a word for an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A girl who is grown up beyond her years has twice become a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice a mother' gives two different words for mother, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a forward, bossy little girl a little madam is an idiom for a precocious child.

clue.text: Editor with aspiration to rise outside the world of mass communications

indicators.note: outside says the reversed aspiration goes round the editor
in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: an aim is an aspiration or goal

explanation.surface: An ambitious editor wants to climb up outside his own paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the press, broadcasting and other means of mass communication.

clue.text: Feature of a passage with a choice of opening movements

definitions.text: Feature of a passage with a choice of opening movements

parts.words: Feature of a passage with a choice of opening movements
parts.note: reads like a piece of music or chess with alternative openings, but describes a door in a corridor that opens either way

explanation.surface: A musical passage or a chess game that allows a choice of openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests music, and 'opening movements' suggests a symphony or chess; it is a corridor door that can be pushed open in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing door is hinged to open both inwards and outwards, often found in corridors.

clue.text: Bulb one splits something not acceptable when lifting

indicators.note: splits says one letter breaks the reversed word in two
in a down clue, lifting means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a no-no is something not allowed or unacceptable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bulb splitting open is unacceptable when being dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a vegetable bulb.

clue.text: Do nought? With such treatment might one make dog useless?

definitions.text: Do nought? With such treatment might one make dog useless?

parts.words: Do nought? With such treatment might one make dog useless?
parts.note: the opening question describes an idle person; the rest suggests that treating the letters of dog with the help of an O for nought produces a word for fine, and that cold treatment makes a hound worthless

explanation.surface: A dog trainer wonders whether letting a dog do nothing will ruin it.
explanation.walkthrough: A layabout does nought; and with a nought (O) added, the letters of dog can be shuffled into a word meaning fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is an idle, worthless person, someone who does nothing useful.

clue.text: What could be "Easy … don't "

parts.note: the quoted words are the start of a calming warning, the kind you say to someone getting carried away

explanation.surface: Someone is told to calm down and not overdo it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots stand for the missing rest of a remark such as 'easy, don't get so excited'; the answer is the spoken phrase that means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady on is a British exclamation urging someone to calm down or not go too far.

clue.text: Female copper

definitions.meaning: a woman's name, a girl called Penelope for short
a copper is a low-value coin, once made of copper

explanation.surface: A woman police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer; here it is a British coin, as the British penny is still called a copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny is a girl's name, and a penny is a small bronze or copper coin.
